messages:
sara: Heads up — our deps scan flagged two Kubernetes-related CVEs that need quick triage: CVE-2026-1024 (kubelet auth bypass) and CVE-2026-2048 (etcd client auth edge case). Also cert-manager CVE-2026-3087 (ACME webhook path traversal) showing up in image scans. Can we decide emergency vs normal maintenance? Potential RBAC tightening and audit gaps to consider. @danny @olivia @mike

 danny: quick take — kubelet one is high if the read-only port or misconfigured kube-proxy exposes it. etctd looks medium. Cert-manager fix exists in 1.12. Do we have clusters with 10255/10250 exposed? I'll run an inventory.

 olivia: prod nodes are on kubelet TLS only, but older staging clusters might have legacy configs. I'll kick off infra-scan (nmap job) and check cluster manifests for kubelet flags. For cert-manager, pinning to 1.12.0 should mitigate ACME issue. Regarding KMS: our cert issuance uses platform KMS key; rotation shouldn't break things but will validate key access for webhook.

 mike: note — audit pipeline had a filter excluding some kubelet.* events since last year (we filtered node-proxy noise). That could hide exploitation attempts. Suggest we relax the filter during the patch window and add temporary retention. Also we should avoid large RBAC changes mid-patch; prefer minimal deny-list change first.

 sara: plan proposal: (1) inventory & exposure check within 4h; (2) emergency hotfix for any exposed clusters within 24h; (3) canary patch (kubelet certs and cert-manager image) in staging → QA → prod rollout; (4) temporary audit filter relaxation + alerting; (5) run RBAC hardening as small, reversible PR. Agree? @deploy-bot check maintenance windows. :eyes:

 deploy-bot: maintenance availability: tonight 02:00-05:00 UTC, tomorrow 23:00-03:00 UTC. No KMS rotations scheduled in next 48h.

 danny: I'll post inventory here when done. If staging shows exposure we'll remediate immediately. For rollback strategy, we should keep previous daemonset images and a node-rollback runbook ready.

 olivia: opening PR for RBAC tweak and audit rule change now — PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4823 (WIP). TL;DR: restrict kubelet exec/attach to system:masters for nodes, and temporarily enable kubelet.auth.* events to central audit. Test plan in PR.

 mike: I'll update audit policy and add alerts for ACME failures and unexpected kubelet auth events. Also enabling high-retention for the next 72h.

 sara: Danny — once inventory is up, share clusters list. Olivia — keep RBAC change minimal and reversible. Mike — monitor closely during canary. I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb in case we need to notify.

 danny: inventory results (short): staging-west-1: kubelet read-only port reachable from within cluster (legacy kube-proxy config), qa-east-2: same. prod: all clusters show no 10255 exposure. I'll kick remediation on staging now.

 deploy-bot: remediation-job:start staging-west-1 at 1959877000

 olivia: remediation completed on staging-west-1 — cert-manager upgraded to 1.12.0, kubelet flag reverted to HTTPS-only, RBAC PR applied in canary namespace. No ACME failures observed in the last 15m.

 mike: audit pipeline now capturing kubelet.auth.* and forwarding to sec-team channel. Set alert if >10 kubelet auth failures in 5m.

 sara: good. Next steps: run QA patch in 30m, then schedule prod maintenance in next available window if QA passes. Create incident ticket for SOC with RBAC delta, KMS verification, and link to runbook.

 danny: added runbook section to infra-runbooks: https://confluence.redwood/platform/runbooks/kubelet-patch (includes rollback commands and cordon/uncordon steps).

 deploy-bot: remediation-job:complete staging-west-1 at 1959877065

 olivia: QA patch started on qa-east-2. Will report status.

 mike: QA shows no ACME issues. Audit spikes normal due to debug filter. Monitoring green.

 sara: thanks all. Follow-up action items: 1) prod maintenance scheduling (danny), 2) finalize RBAC PR (olivia), 3) SOC ticket + KMS confirm (sara/mike). We'll reconvene if QA shows regressions. :thumbsup:
